sections.trivia:
The game was an all ticket game with tickets going on sale two weeks prior. all the tickets for the enclosure and ground were sold with a capacity set at 35,000.
Nottingham Forest made a bid of £312,000 for Bertie Auld. The player was happy at Celtic and as such the matter was dropped.
Sparta Rotterdam manager Denis Neville watched the game from the Celtic stand. Sparta Rotterdam were due to play Rangers in the quarter final of the European Cup in March.
Despite all the Celtic players being declared fit the one change from the previous team was the inclusion of Bobby Carroll at centre forward replacing John Colrain. Davis at right half for Rangers was declared fit but Ian McMillan and Alec Scott lost out.
sections.review:
A goal half a minute from the end gave Rangers their fifth successive win against Celtic. The goal came when Bobby Evans headed out only to Baird who passed through to Millar who hit a shot high and hard into the roof of the net past an advancing Haffey. Celtic appealed that Millar had been offside when receiving the pass but the goal stood. Just before Niven missed Carroll’s shot and Davis was forced to clear off the Rangers line. Fifteen minutes into the second half Haffey had saved a Rangers penalty pushing the spot kick from Little out for a corner. the penalty came when Jim Kennedy clearly handled a goal bound shot.
Other than these incidents the game was noted as being mediocre in the forwards with dreadful passing partly caused by the soft ground and treacherous conditions underfoot.

sections.trivia:
Following the late 1-0 loss to Rangers in the Glasgow derby the day before, Celtic travelled to Edinburgh to take on the league leaders. Hearts had handed out a 5-1 whupping to Hibernian the day before and played an unchanged side.
Celtic switched the front line with Bobby Carroll switching to outside right and Auld going to his favoured outside left and Alec Byrne going to centre forward.
This was the third successive loss for Celtic and they dropped to twelth in the table.
sections.review:
Celtic started well but it was Hearts that took the lead after just six minutes with a well executed goal with Bauld centring for Smith to head home. Bertie Auld was getting the better of Kirk and having a great game. In the 37th minute Bertie Peacock hit a flyer of an equaliser from thirty yards that marshall did not even move for. 
The second half continued as the first with Celtic looking classy and all to play for. But in the 60th minute Bauld met a Bowman cross to head home and Celtic started to flag after fighting so hard. To add further injury Hearts were awarded a penalty on 72 minutes and despite all Haffey's attempts Thomson made it three.

sections.trivia:
Both McNeill and Auld who had picked up ankle knocks in the previous game against Raith Rovers, were out. In came Crerand and Divers for them. Also in came John Kurila for a first start of the season for Bobby Evans, who appeared to have picked up a knee injury during training in the week, and Dan O'Hara replaced Eric Smith, who was also unfit, at inside right. For Clyde Clinton was out at left half. Tommy Ring, Clyde's international winger also failed to start as he was about to be transferred to Everton, however they played a new man in 20 year old John McLaughlin who was originallty from Clydebank and about to be demobbed from the Army.
In the previous week Celtic had made an attempt to sign Jack Mudie from Blackpool. Mudie, and experienced inside forward had been scoring goals but was in dispute with Blackpool and it was thouight that he would be the person to put some added steel into the forward line. Blackpool however replied that he was not for sale after an air-clearing meeting.
Celtic announced the arrangement of a floodlit night Friendly game against Everton for the 27th January. The game would see the return to Celtic Park of Bobby Collins, sold to Everrton for £24,000 in September 1958.
This was only John Kurila's second full game for the first team and he acquitted himself well and showed the great promise available for the future. Speculation was rife that if Everton were not ssful in signing Tommy Ring then Celtic would step in with a bid. Certainly there seemed to be a realisatioin that the team needed strengthening with experience.
sections.review:
New start for Clyde, John McLaughlin turned out to be some find scoring twice and setting up another. Alec Byrne got two for Celtic with Neil Mochan converting an early penalty to leave the score even at 3-3.
In the fourth minute Finlay fouled O'Hara for a penalty which was calmly dispatched by Mochan in his usual manner. Back came Clyde and McLaughlin scored his first from a header from a turned back ball from Shearer. A period of end-to-end football followed but McLaughlin was having a star game for Clyde and he beat Haffey again but not the crossbar in the 18th minute. McLaughlin made Clyde's second goal when he crossed for Robertson to shoot home. Byrne equalised not long after from a Divers cross. Clyde were not finished and Robertson and McLaughlin again combined. At half time it was 3-2 with all to play for in what was turning out to be a good game.
The second half continued fast. Celtic eventually got an equaliser when Byrne bundled the ball in. A decent game between two well-matched sides.

The possibility of Tommy Ring ex of Clyde joining Celtic was finally killed when the player signed for Everton for £12,000. Speculation now linked Celtic with out-of-favour Hearts player Ian Crawford.
Back in came an uninjured and 'flu-recovered Bobby Evans for the young John Kurila. Auld, McNeill and Smith were still out nursing injuries but on the road to recovery.
Heavy snow fell in Scotland this week with trains being marooned and roads closed.
Arbroath were newly promoted to Division 1 this season and were having a pretty torrid time of it having won only four times at home in 22 games. They were rooted to the bottom of the table and already looking like relegation candidates, though Stirling Albion were doing their best to give them a contender for that accolade.
In outside news, BMC announced the building of a new commercial vehicle plant to be built at Bathgate which would employ up to 5,600 people.

Five minutes from half time Byrne scored with a mighty left foot shot. O'Hara had a goal disallowed for some infringement at the start of the second half. Carroll got the tird from a Mochan pass and Divers finished it with his second just before the final whistle.

sections.trivia:
The Scotland team to face the Scottish League on 2nd February was announced. Bobby Evans was selected as captain and centre half. Frank Haffey was also selected as reserve goalkeeper. Duncan MacKay was listed for the Scottish League. In the end neither MacKay or Evans played but Haffey was in goal for Sctland in a 2-2 draw.
The game was interesting for Everton's Anglo-Scots who would have a chance to change the minds of the Scotland selectors. Parker at right back duly impressed the selectors and played himself into the Scotland team. 
Jimmy McGrory stated that he would field his strongest side. As such an unchanged side from the one that had beaten Arbroath 40-0 was fielded. 
Stirling Albion manager Alex McCrae made a bid to take John Colrain to the Binos. Colrain was stuill considered a Celtic centre forward but he was out of the first team of late and travelling reserve.
The teams had last met in the 1938 Exhibition Cup Final, when Celtic had also won by the same score.
sections.review: A large crowd turned up for this rather dull game. What had been expected was a fast and active Everton but they appeared to be running at half speed. Haffey, Evans and Crerand played well and Crerand and MacKay were able to snuff out Everton's Anglo-Scottish left side attack of Collins and Ring. The goal came from a Neil Mochan cross which Carroll met on the volley the ball going in off the underside of the bar and the far post

sections.review:
Aberdeen started fast and had the better of the early exchanges. Celtic gradually got back into the game. Celtic opened the scoring from the penalty spot when Mochan was brought down by Kinnell. Smiler took the spot kick himself and scored. Five minutes later Aberdeen were level when Kinnell placed a strong shot from a free kick past Haffey.

The Dons went ahead after 52 minutes when Haffey failed toi cut out a cross and Davidson headed home. Davidson was booked not long after. Celtic got a second penalty for another infringement against Mochan and he converted the kick again. With it all level Brownlee found a winner for the Dons with 2 minutes to go.

Snow had fallen during the week and the teams came out to a ground speckled with both snow and sand and frozen underfoot. This led to difficult playing conditions with the ball bouncing all over the place.
sections.review:
A solid game with two evenly matched teams. Bobby Evans had a fairly torrid game by his standards. Despite good attempts from both sides it remained 0-0 at the break. 
Baker and Colrain were the two stand-outs on either side – Baker with some magnioficent shooting (well matched by Haffey's saving) and Colrain for his boundless energy and non-stop trying. On 57 minutes the Buddies got their reward when from a free kick conceded by McNeill the ball was lofted in and Baker hit the crossbar with Rodger picking up the rebound and heading home. That lead stood for all of 45 seconds as Byrne took off straight from the kick off and scored with a mighty shot with hardly any back lift. Buddies right half lately a target of Rangers, was then booked for one-too-many trip on an opposing player.

This was the replay of the 1-1 draw played on the Saturday at Love Street. The game was on the Wednesday night with a 7:30 pm kick off. Though the pitch was playable on the Tuesday, overnight snow and frost made the pitch unplayable of the Wednesday and the game was delayed for a further week. sections.review:
With the fixture complications due to the weather there was a push to get this game on. Mochan scored first but back came St Mirren to hold a 3-1 lead at half time. Urged on by Mocan Celtic drew level with goals from Divers and Mochan. This took the game to extra time. In the eigth minute kennedy went to clear a ball for it to ricochet of Bryceland and trickle into the net. Celtic threw everything at St Mirren and Divers equalised again to take the game to a further replay.
With the availability of a neutral ground uncertain both managers tossed for the rights to hold the game and Jimmy McGrory won.The game would be played on the next night

This much postponed game was finally played on this Monday night. sections.review:
After an epic struggle in this round of the Cup the Bhoys finally came thru in dramatic style with Neil Mochan getting all five goals. The St Mirren rejig did nothing to add to their team and they found themselves constantly exposed to the speed of Colrain and Divers. Mochan too played like a rejuvenated man and gave Tierney a night to forget. He could have had a further three goals but for excellent keeping from Walker. The song of the night was 'When the Saints go marching out!'
The management took the players to Seamills to unwind for two days following this game.

sections.review:
Described by the ever 'loyal' Gair Henderson in the Evening Times as '…a let off for Celtic'.
Very much a partisan home highland crowd with only 700 travelling Celtic support. Elgin started well and it required all the attention of Evans to snap out several attacks. Celtic's attack finally started and Divers and Mochan both had attempts. Elgin played a high line and Celtic's forwards were being caught offside when the breaks occurred. Jenkins too, in the Elgin goal was having a hero's day making wonder saves from Colrain and Smith to keep it goalless. 
The second half saw Elgin City come out with real belief that they could win the tie and Celtic were pinned back. This valiant effort had taken its toll and with the highlanders visibly tiring Celtic began to get more of the game. Celtic however had reverted to the profligates in front of goal that they had been at the start of the season. Even Mochan missed with a shot that seemed to be a certain goal. Elgin got their just desserts on 65 minutes when Grant scored from a shot parried by Haffey. Cue highland madness. 
However it was not to be. In a tacticalitch pushed on by bertie Peacock, Eric Smith moved over to the left, switching with Alec Byrne and started to combine well with Divers. Divers went on to score from a Smith cross and just before the end Smith fired home a suoperb shot to get Celtic out of the highland jail.

sections.review:
Auld and Smith on the right side played well together and were responsible for a number of good moves. It was their passing movement which led to the goal, Conway firing past Muirhead. Celtic continued to be dominant in the first half without adding to the score. Hibs came out more determined in the second half and Haffey was called on to keep a clean sheet several times. Smith and Conway had chances to increase the lead but failed.
A hard fought game with little in it but few failures on both sides.

sections.trivia:
Celtic were drawn against Rangers in the semi final of the Scottish Cup. The game was to be played at Hampden Park. The other semi was between Clyde and Kilmarnock. An initial 30,000 griound cap was placed but this was soon revived to 90,000 as the game was at Hampden, but the game would be all-ticket
Bertie Auld was out following his ankle injury in the cup against Partick Thistle. Also succumbing to the back injury was Neil Mochan. His place was taken by Jim Conway and finally Billy McNeill had to withdraw with an ankle injury and his place was taken by Pat Crerand.
An agreement was reached finally between the television companies and the SFA on the live televising of games. The argument had been rumbling on for some time and in best SFA traditions a separate sub-committee had been set up to investigate the whole matter. The following proposals were put to the BBC and STV and appeared to be agreed by the television companies:-

No indications of the games or the scores to be made before 5:00 pm
The TV companies needed to spread the televised games around all the clubs, not just the most attractive fixtures
A review of the upcoming Saturay football should be screened on Friday evening.
The senior SFA representative on the negotiations was Mr Robert Kelly, the Celtic chairman. In his opinion there should be NO televising of games at all.
The biggest news though was the move of Jock Stein from Reserve Coach at Celtic to become the new manager at Dunfermiline./ Dunfermiline were next to bottom in Division 1 and had sacked their manager McRae. Jock Stein took the job on to keep them up and immediately put every player at the club on trial on the Monday evening that he took over.
This game was played on the Wednesday night and marked the start of a busy period for Celtic with four games in 10 days.
Denis Law was transferred from Huddersfield Town to manchester City for an alleged fee of £53,000.
sections.review: A poor game by all accounts with both goals coming from half backs from free kicks. Celtic had the better midfield but Bobby Evans had a less than good second half and allowed the Ayr centre Price in several times. Ayr’s goal came from a back-heeled free kick which Willie McIntyre rocketed home. Celtic’s goal came from a Crerand free on the edge of the box after Paterson had handled.

Two minutes later melrose completed almost an identiocal manoeuvre to put the Pars 3-1 up. Byrne picked up another goal for Celtic after a Conway breakawy and shot was palmed out to him and he put the ball away.

sections.trivia:
Bertie Auld remained out and it might be for some time. The ankle injury proved to be more sever than thought and he was in plaster.
The Reserves played Rangers in the Second XI Cup semi final at Ibrox. The team was Connor, Donnelly, Upton, Crerand, Kurila, Clark, Carroll, Jackson, Lochhead, Gallacher, Chalmers. They were beaten 2-0 by Rangers reserves.
Bobby Evans captained The Scottish League against the English League at Highbury on 23rd March losing 1-0. Evans had a stand out game. He was back home and in the side for this game despite having taken a head knock at Highbury, with Crerand giving way and McNeill dropping bnack to right half. In came Jim Conway for Alec Byrne on the left wing.
Stirling Albion were involved in a desperate fight to stay up along with Aberdeen and Dunfermiline. Celtic had just been beaten by Dunfermiline.
The Scottish League ruled in Celtic's favour to play Third Lanark on the Monday night following this game. Third Lanark wanted the Tuesday as they had arranged a Reserve game against Rangers Reserves on the Monday night. With the impending Cup game against Rangers following, Celtic wanted the maximum tiome to prepare.
sections.review: A frustrating and poor game for Celtic. Despite being in a relegation scrap Stirling Albion too were pretty lethargic. Conway looked half the player he could be and even Evans had a poor game by his standards. Celtic missed a penalty in the 17th minute after Mochan was brought down in the area. His spot kick was hit wide by two feet. Even so Mochan was the best of the forwards. Haffey was at odds for the Bino's goal – not the first time this season.

sections.trivia:
Played on the Monday night as a floodlit game.This was a postponed fixture from earluier in the season.
Evans was rested for this game with the usual arrangement of Billy McNeill moving to centre and Pat Crerand coming in at right half. Back in came Alec Byrne for the lacklustre Conway and also in for Divers was Stevie Chalmers. Divers had picked up an ankle injury.
There was much speculation regarding Celtic signing wing half Johnny Kelly from Crewe Alexandra. Kelly had previously played for Third Lanark. He was duly signed on the 30th March.
sections.review: Celtic made up for the lethargy shown in the previous outing against Stirling Albion and started this one straight out the traps. Mochan was the player on form making three goals and scoring from the penalty spot. The passing was fast and accurate and was the making of Colrain and Chalmer's first goals. Mochan dummied a Smith pass for Colrain to get the first. Both Smith and Byne hit the posts in the first half.  Neil laid on the pass for Chalmers to get his first goal and after the break he laid on an accurate pass from the byeline for Chalmers to get his second. Robb handled the ball in the area for the Celtic penalty but by that time Celtic had taken their foot off the gas.

sections.trivia:
Scotland announced the team to face England at Hampden on 9th April. Duncan MacKay and Bobby Evans were selected. MacKay was also selected for the U23s to face Belgium on 20th April along with Frank Haffey and Billy McNeill.
Rangers had just come off of winning the quarter final replay European cup game against Sparta Rotterdam and were set up for a European Cup semi final against Eintracht Frankfurt.
Eric Smith was out having suffered a head injury in a car crash during the previous week. In came Stevie Chalmers and back came John Divers who had recovered from the ankle knock that had kept him out against Third Lanark.
In the other semi final played at Ibrox Kilmarnock beat Clyde 2-0 to contest their second Scottish Cup in four years.
sections.review:
After initial clashes this settled down in the first half to a series of midfield skirmishes with both sets of half backs going turn and turn about. In the 25th minute Celtic won a corner taken by Colrain. The ball sailed over and Chalmers took a mighty leap to head home for Celtic. Rangers threw everything at the Celtic goal but also had to survive an excellent header from Divers.
Rangers came out for the second half with the wind at their backs and proceeded to camp in the Celtic half searching for the equaliser. Celtic's forwards were dangerous whenever they saw the ball, no more so than Mochan. Rangers equaliser arrived in the 68th minute from a Millar header. Celtic desperately held out for the final twenty minutes.

sections.trivia:
The replay of the semi final at Hampden Park on the Wednesday with a 4:30pm kick off following the 1-1 draw on Saturday
Celtic had Alec Byrne out from the original game team. He had been nursing a groin strain since the St Mirren Cup replay. In came Mike Jackson for a return to the first team after making a good run at the start of the season. Meanwhile for Rangers goalkeeper Niven was out with a back strain.
Rangers had never defeated Celtic in a Scottish Cup replay.
The SFA gave Celtic permission to play a Friendly against Sparta Rotterdam on the 14th May as the culmination of Dutch Week in Glasgow. Sparta wanted to play the other half of Glasgow after being beaten by Rangers after a replay in the European Cup quarter finals.
sections.review: A day really for Jimmy Millar, the Rangers centre forward, who gave Bobby Evans a torrid time all game. The first half though was pretty even and a first goal by Wilson was equalised by Mochan on 33 minutes with the Celtic forwards then looking quite dominant with Ritchie having to make good saves from Colrain and McNeill. After the interval however, Rangers found their man in Millar. Four minutes into the second half he put Rangers ahead. Celtic's defense fell apart in the second half and a further two goals followed. For the last 14 minutes Rangers were down to 10 men when Davis was stretchered off, Baird going to right half.

sections.trivia:
Scotland played England at Hampden on 9th April drawing 1-1. Frank Haffey, Duncan MacKay and Bobby Evans all played for Scotland.
For Celtic Frank Haffey was out injured allowing Fallon back between the sticks; on the left wing in came Charie Gallacher for his second start of the season.
sections.review:
A meagre 5,000 turned up to watch this Tuesday evening game. 
Despite the usual array of backs and half backs barring Fallon in goal the defense was strangely ill at ease. Celtic started well and efforts by Mochan, Colrain and Chalmers were well saved by Freebairn. Evans appeared to have trouble with the speed of Smith. On 20 minutes Fallon was beaten by a shot from McParland. After that the Jags passing was smoother and their defense coped adequately with any Celtic attack. In the second half Colrain went to the wing with Chalmers moving inside. A Kennedy pass back was intercepted by Smith who easily made it two for Partick. Smith then helped himself to two further goals with his spped and intelligent service from McKenzie. All the Celtic players looked out of sorts barring Stevie Chalmers who got both the Celtic goals late on.

sections.trivia:
Hearts wrapped up the league flag this weekend with a darw against St Mirren. With two games to play Hearts were 5 points ahead of Kilmarnock and could not be overtaken.
Scotland chose 18 players to tour Europe in May following the close of the season in Scotland. Included for Celtic were Duncan MacKay and Bobby Evans.
Frank Haffey was fit again after his back strain and returned in goal; John Divers paid the pernalty for the abject display against Partick Thistle and was dropped in favour of Bobby Carroll coming in at outside right and John Colrain moving to Divers position at inside left.
sections.review:
The sides started fairly evenly with shots at either end. Dundee went ahead when a fairly innocuous looking pass got through to Gilzean on the penalty spot and he fired home. Celtic came back strongly and despite good efforts from Colrain and Mochan could not beat Liney in the Dundee goal. Then just before the interval Robertson collected another pass which should have been cut out and beat Haffey from in close.

In the second half goalkeeper Frank Haffey was carried off and taken to hospital following a collision with Dunky MacKay. Bobby Evans went into goal at 2-0 down and kept a clean sheet for the remainder of the game. With a man down Celtic were under pressure and failed to find an answer to the two Dundee goals from the first half.

With Haffey suffering still from the effects of concussion after his collision with MacKay at Dundee, John Fallon again found himself back in goal. Johnny Divers was also restored to inside left with John Colrain dropping out.
sections.review:
Celtic went ahead when Welsh and Mochan both went up to head a free kick and the ball slid off the Airdrie man and beat Beaton in goal. Airdrie pulled one back through Rankin from a Stewart pass and ex-Celt Jim Sharkey nearly put Airdrie ahead shortly before half time.
Airdrie started the second period well with Fallon having to make a good save from Ormond before Stewart beat him with a shot. Mochan equalised on 65 minutes with a shot from a Crerand throw in. Now at level pegging Airdrie appeared to collapse and Stevie Chalmers scored three goals, the pick being his second, a crisp 18 yard shot.

sections.trivia:
Twelve day gap between this and the previous game, with the Scottish Cup Final between Kilmarnock and Rangers on the intervening weekend. Rangers duly won with a 2-0 result. 
This was the last League game of the season.
The Reserves duly won the Reserve League Championship for the second year in succession.
Arbroath and Stirling Albion were relegated from Division 1 for next season and St Johnstone and Dundee Utd were promoted from Division 2.
Bertie Auld passed a fitness test on the 23d April and went on in a reserve game to gain match fitness. He had been out with an ankle injury sustained in the Cup win against Partick Thistle on the 12th March.
sections.review:
Celtic got off to the best of starts when after good play Mochan cooly lobbed the keeper for the first goal. After much Celtic pressure and squandered chances, Chalmers got the second on 33 minutes with a solid shot and followed that up eight minutes later with Celtic's third, when he slipped the ball past the goalkeeper following a corner.
The second half pace was a little brisker than the start-stop action of the first half. Evans and Baker were having a good tussle and up front for Celtic, Mochan proved to be the handful for the Saints defense. With twelve minutes left to play Gemmell pulled one back for St Mirren closely followed by a goal from Baker. With their tails up St Mirren pushed for an equaliser which duly arrived from Miller.

sections.trivia:
The second of the First Round ties – the first was between Third lanark and Queen's Park with Third Lanark coming out 3-0 winners. 
Robert Kelly was appointed president of the SFA on the 4th May, succeeding John Park of Queen's Park. Also on the 4th May Scotland were beaten by Poland at Hampden Park. Duncan MacKay and Bobby Evans played for Scotland with Evans as usual captain. 
On the 6th May it was announced that Bobby Evans would leave Celtic. Evans had asked to be put on the transfer list when re-contracting time came round and the Celtic directors reluctantly agreed to his wish. Bobby Evans had been with the club for 16 years.
sections.review: Clyde must have thought the tie was all over when they scored a third goal without reply on 54 minutes. It took that long for the Celtic attack to wake up. What followed was a revival and first Bertie Auld scored followed by the now regular goal addition from Neil Mochan and to finish off bertie Peacock got a captain's goal. With the game tied at 3-3 on 90 minutes the result was made by a toss of the coin with Celtic progressing to the semi final against Rangers.

sections.review:
Rangers were poor but physical and Celtic profligate and amiss in their shooting as well as unlucky. Rangers had Scott pretty much out of the game from ten minutes to half time when he collided with Fallon and Kennedy. Fallon also picked up a leg injury which hampered him. Crerand's goal was a thing of beauty, chesting a clearance down and weaving his way past three Rangers players before shooting home. Celtic showed the better team spirit but too many were intimidated by the ball-or-man tactics adopted by Rangers and overrall the game was poor.
With the game level after 90 minutes the result was decided by a toss of the coin and Caldow called it correct for Rangers.

sections.review: The Dutch team were much changed from the side that had faced Rangers in the European Cup quarter final earlier in the season. They also had to return to a further league game in Holland 24 hours after this game. Celtic started fast and gave the Dutch defenders no rest. Chalmers scored the best of the goals. Billy McNeill, Chalmers and Crerand all played well.
